annotations.title: Entrances
annotations.lead: There are two entrances to the crew cabin, a main entrance on the side and one at the apex (narrow) end of the command module.

annotations.title: Side Hatch
annotations.lead: In flight, the side opening through the pressure vessel and command module heat shield is sealed by a single "unified" hatch (not currently attached).

annotations.title: Docking Tunnel
annotations.lead: The passageway to and from the lunar module is at the apex (narrow) end of the command module.

annotations.title: Forward Hatch
annotations.lead: The forward, or docking hatch is a combined pressure and insulating hatch mounted at the top of the docking tunnel.

annotations.title: Guidance and Navigation Station (G&N)
annotations.lead: G&N instruments and controls are located in lower equipment bay.

annotations.title: Environment System Controls
annotations.lead: Manual controls for environmental systems are located in the left-hand equipment bay.

annotations.title: Waste Management Systems Controls
annotations.lead: Columbia's waste management system along with several non-time-critical circuit breakers for other systems.

annotations.title: Storage Lockers
annotations.lead: Storage lockers of various sizes are distributed throughout the cabin, including in the aft section underneath the astronaut couches.

annotations.title: Columbia's Interior
annotations.lead: Designed to house and protect three crew members and their equipment during the trip to and from lunar orbit.

annotations.title: Crew Couches
annotations.lead: Couches help position the crew as they work on tasks during the mission.

annotations.title: Rotation and Translation Controls
annotations.lead: Located on the armrests of two crew couches

annotations.title: Lunar Module Pilot Controls
annotations.lead: Opposite the right-hand seat, facing systems controls.

annotations.title: Displays and Controls
annotations.lead: Displays and controls used in Apollo include meters and switches that allow the flight crew to monitor and control the operations of the spacecraft.

annotations.title: Pilot Controls
annotations.lead: Opposite the center seat, facing flight and systems controls.

annotations.title: Commander's Controls
annotations.lead: Opposite the left-hand seat, facing the flight controls.

annotations.title: Toggle Switches
annotations.lead: Toggle switches are the most frequently used type of controls on Columbia.

annotations.title: Pushbutton Switches
annotations.lead: Pushbuttons were most widely used where astronauts needed to initiate a spacecraft function quickly.

annotations.title: Rotary Switches
annotations.lead: Rotary switches were used on the control panel when four or more set positions were required to control discrete functions.

annotations.title: Continuously-Variable Controls
annotations.lead: Used for functions requiring precise control and adjustment.  These included control of lighting intensities, audio volume, and antenna positioning.

annotations.title: Flight Director/Attitude Indicator
annotations.lead: The flight director attitude indicator (FDAI), was the primary flight display.

annotations.title: Entry Monitor System
annotations.lead: A guidance package used to monitor performance during thrusting, rendezvous, and re-entry maneuvers.

annotations.title: Display and Keyboard Assembly, or DSKY
annotations.lead: Used to communicate with command module's guidance computer.

annotations.title: Navigating from the Command Module
annotations.lead: Guidance computer programs required precise fixes on stars or other visual features.

annotations.title: A Hand-Drawn Calendar
annotations.lead: Small calendar drawn on the lower equipment bay wall.

annotations.title: Epitaph to a Journey
annotations.lead: A note by Michael Collins, written over 50 years ago, beautifully conveys a sentiment we all have to appreciate now more than ever.
